purpose: Sources for glossary definitions, kept apart from data/citations.json on purpose. That file is the REVIEWED REPORT SEED: src/lib/claims/canonical-report-data.test.ts pins it at exactly 71 claims and 19 citations against a fixed 2026-09-06 commit date, and src/lib/claims/registry.ts requires every entry to be used by a report claim. A glossary definition is not a report claim, so a source only a definition uses is an orphan by that model's own definition — and adding one would mean re-pinning content that represents a completed review. Two registers with one shape each is safer than one register with two meanings.
rule: Every entry needs a snapshot under docs/sources/, an access date, and a quote of at most 25 words that scripts/glossary/fetch-source.mjs verified is present in the fetched bytes. Every entry must be referenced by a definition in data/jargon.json, and every citationId there must resolve here. Both directions are checked by scripts/claims-gate.ts.

citations.identifier: NHGRI Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms: Carrier
citations.quote: an individual who carries and is capable of passing on a genetic mutation associated with a disease
citations.claim: Supports the wording of Inherit's glossary definition for this term and nothing else. Not a clinical statement, not a claim about any person's file, not an endorsement of any Inherit result.

citations.identifier: NHGRI Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms: Susceptibility
citations.quote: refers to the state of being predisposed to, or sensitive to, developing a certain disease
citations.claim: Supports the wording of Inherit's glossary definition for this term and nothing else. "Predisposed to" carries Inherit's "a tendency toward an outcome"; the definition's "not a certain result" is that same fact stated negatively, not an extra claim the page is being read to make. Not a clinical statement, not a claim about any person's file, not an endorsement of any Inherit result.

citations.identifier: CDC Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, Lesson 3 Section 2: Morbidity Frequency Measures
citations.quote: Number of new cases of disease during specified time interval
citations.claim: Supports the wording of Inherit's glossary definition for this term and nothing else. The quote is the numerator CDC gives for incidence proportion in Table 3.3; its denominator on the same row is the population at the start of the interval, which is the "in a group" half of Inherit's definition. Not a clinical statement, not a claim about any person's file, not an endorsement of any Inherit result.

citations.identifier: CDC Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, Lesson 3 Section 2: Morbidity Frequency Measures
citations.quote: the proportion of an initially disease-free population that develops disease, becomes injured, or dies during a specified (usually limited) period of time
citations.claim: Supports the wording of Inherit's glossary definition for this term and nothing else. CDC names this measure incidence proportion and lists "risk" among its synonyms on the same page, which is why it carries Inherit's "absolute risk" rather than a page using that exact phrase. Not a clinical statement, not a claim about any person's file, not an endorsement of any Inherit result.
